sections.h2: Where is Clayton County, Iowa, and what is the land like?
sections.html:
Clayton County is in the northeast corner of Iowa along the Mississippi River, and at roughly 792 square miles it is the fifth largest county in the state by area. Elkader is the county seat.

The county touches Allamakee, Winneshiek, Fayette, Buchanan, Delaware and Dubuque counties in Iowa, and across the river it faces Crawford and Grant counties in Wisconsin. It lies in the Driftless Area, which was missed by the last ice sheet, so streams have cut deep valleys and the Mississippi is edged with bluffs.

That terrain shapes real estate. A house on a ridge, in a river valley or on the flat land by the Mississippi has very different weather and flood exposure, even within a few miles.

sections.h2: What are the main towns in Clayton County?
sections.html:
Clayton County is almost entirely rural, with 99.1 percent of residents living in rural areas in 2020, and its towns are small. The 2020 census counted these places.

Postville (partly in Allamakee County)2,503
Guttenberg1,817

Elkader (county seat)1,209

The county's total was 17,043 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 16,845. Its record was 28,829 in 1880.

Clayton County was formed on December 21, 1837, and named for John M. Clayton, a Delaware senator who later served as Secretary of State under Zachary Taylor.

Guttenberg on the river was the first county seat, from 1838 to 1843. German immigrants arrived there from 1845, and between 1845 and 1865 builders put up more than one hundred limestone buildings, many still standing in the Front Street Historic District. Elkader was platted and incorporated in 1846 and is named for the Algerian leader Emir Abdelkader.

Elkader's Keystone Bridge over the Turkey River, built of local sandstone, is described as the largest stone arch bridge west of the Mississippi.

sections.h2: Who lives in Clayton County, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 put the median value of owner-occupied homes in Clayton County at $168,500, with 78.0 percent of households owning. Median household income was $67,242.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 8,890
  • Persons per household: 2.23
  • Bachelor's degree or higher, age 25+: 14.5%
  • Guttenberg median age in 2020: 55.6, with 34.1% of residents 65 or older
  • Postville median age in 2020: 29.4, with about 35% under 18

sections.h2: What drives the Clayton County economy?
sections.html:
Farming, small manufacturing and meat processing carry most of the local economy. Postville is the clearest example: Agri Star Meat and Poultry employed about 700 people as of 2017, more than 30 percent of the town's population, and Norplex-Micarta has made laminated plastic products there since 1975.

Guttenberg began as a river trading town, with lead mining on Miners Creek and a flour mill. After the Civil War, railroads and an interior road system reduced its role as a regional market center.

Roads follow the same pattern. US 52 runs through Guttenberg, and Postville sits where US 18 and US 52 meet Iowa Highway 51. School districts include Central Community (Elkader), Clayton Ridge (Guttenberg and Garnavillo, merged in 2005), and Postville Community.

sections.h2: What weather and flood risks matter for a Clayton County house?
sections.html:
Clayton County has a documented flood record on two rivers. The National Weather Service lists record crests of 27.77 feet on the Turkey River at Elkader on June 10, 2008, where flood stage is 12 feet, and 23.65 feet on the Mississippi at Guttenberg on April 24, 1965, where flood stage is 15 feet.

June 2008 brought 3 to 7 inches of rain over two days, closed roads with mudslides and caused more than $10 million in property damage. Guttenberg's riverfront flooded many times, and a levee was built after 1965.

  • 14 documented tornadoes since 1950, including an F3 west of Elkader on May 30, 1985
  • 102 reports of large hail and 104 damaging wind reports since 1982
  • Average Elkader snowfall of about 37 inches per season, and a record low of minus 47 degrees on February 3, 1996

For a seller, a flood history can lead to insurance questions, and an older roof raises hail and wind questions.

sections.h2: Which Clayton County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The county's property tax offices are in Elkader. The Treasurer's office is at 111 High Street NE, Suite 102, Elkader, IA 52043, phone 563-245-1106, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

The county site lists a second building at 600 Gunder Road NE, and its assessor page does not give a separate assessor phone, so use the county contact page. The assessor values property, the auditor calculates levies, and the treasurer collects.

sections.h2: When are Clayton County property taxes due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Taxes are billed in two installments, due September 1 and March 1. The county says the first half penalty starts October 1, or 30 days after the auditor certifies to the treasurer if that is later, and the second half penalty starts April 1.

ItemClayton County rule
Penalty rate1 1/2% per month on real estate tax
Tax saleThird Monday in June, 1:00 p.m.
Advertising fee$4.00 per attached description
Certificate fee if sold$10.00
Redemption interest2% per month, minimum $1.00

Iowa Code 445.37 sets the state rule for mailed payments: the treasurer must receive a non-electronic payment by the last business day of the month before the delinquent date, or it must be postmarked before that date.

sections.h2: How are Clayton County homes assessed and protested?
sections.html:
Clayton County assesses non-agricultural property at 100 percent of market value as of January 1, and the assessor must reassess everything in odd numbered years, with notices due by April 15. Farm dwellings are valued like other houses, while farm land is valued by productivity, and mobile homes are taxed per square foot.

The county's assessment page lists a protest period of April 16 to May 5, but Iowa Code 441.37 says April 2 to April 30, so check with the office before relying on either date. The board sits through May, and if an equalization order changes values it meets again from October 15 to November 15.

Accepted grounds include inequity with similar property, a value above market, an exempt or misclassified property and an assessment error. A board decision can go to the Property Assessment Appeal Board and then to district court within 20 days after the appeal letter is postmarked. An owner can also go straight to district court within 20 days after the board adjourns or by May 31, whichever is later.

sections.h2: What should a Clayton County seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
Taxes are normally prorated between buyer and seller, and the closing statement shows each share. The county treasurer sends statements to the titleholder of record, so the seller should forward any bill that arrives after closing.

State transfer tax is 80 cents per $500 above the first $500, and a declaration of value signed by a seller or buyer goes in with the deed. The assessor receives it and keeps it for three years.

A seller with back taxes should clear them before the June sale, since a sold certificate adds interest at 2 percent per month and fees to the payoff.

faqs.q: When are Clayton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. The county adds a 1 1/2 percent monthly penalty from October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Clayton County?
faqs.a: Pay at the County Treasurer, 111 High Street NE, Suite 102, Elkader, or call 563-245-1106. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: When is the Clayton County tax sale?
faqs.a: The tax sale is held on the third Monday of June at 1:00 p.m. A $4.00 advertising fee applies before the sale and $10.00 is added per certificate if a parcel sells.

faqs.q: What is the protest deadline in Clayton County?
faqs.a: State law sets April 2 to April 30, while the county's assessment page lists April 16 to May 5. Confirm the current dates with the office before you file.
The NWS lists record floods on the Turkey River at Elkader in June 2008 and on the Mississippi at Guttenberg in April 1965. Check a property's flood zone before you list.
